provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Food family batch. Two businesses in one category: weekly meal prep sells on subscriptions and cut-offs, private chefs sell on trust and a booking step. No nutrition or health outcome claims anywhere. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Weekly meal rotation and order cut-off
pageStructurePlus.contains: This week's rotating meals, the order-by day and time, delivery or pickup day, portion sizes, and a countdown so nobody misses the weekly cut-off
pageStructurePlus.why: Meal prep customers order on a weekly rhythm. The cut-off is the single fact they need most, and missing it loses a week's order.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Meals-per-week options, per-meal price the owner sets, how to skip a week, pause for travel or cancel, and when cards are charged
pageStructurePlus.why: Subscribers decide on how easy it is to pause and cancel. Clear rules up front turn a trial week into a standing order.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Calories, protein, carbs and fat per meal as calculated by the chef, plus plan styles like high-protein, plant-based or low-carb, with no health promises
pageStructurePlus.why: Gym-goers and busy professionals choose meal prep by macros and plan style. They compare labels before they compare prices.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Neighbourhoods and zip codes covered, delivery windows by zone, gym or studio pickup points, cooler bag drop-off, and what happens when nobody's home
pageStructurePlus.why: The first question from a new meal prep customer is whether you deliver to them. A zone map answers it before they leave.

pageStructurePlus.section: Private chef dinners and in-home cooking
pageStructurePlus.contains: Dinner parties, date nights and weekly in-home cooking, what the chef brings, how groceries are billed, the kitchen the chef needs and the consultation step
pageStructurePlus.why: Private chef clients are letting someone into their kitchen. They hire the chef whose process feels clear and trustworthy before the first call.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How long each meal keeps in the fridge, oven and microwave reheating steps, freezing notes, and the reusable container return or deposit program
pageStructurePlus.why: New meal prep customers worry about what happens after the bag arrives. Clear reheating and storage notes head off most of the first week's support messages.

openers.line: Your meal prep business has a Google listing and no website, so someone searching for weekly meal delivery can't see this week's menu or the order cut-off.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what would sit behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Orders on a generic survey form
openers.line: Meal prep orders go through a generic survey form that doesn't show prices or totals. Customers want to see their weekly meal order add up before they commit.
openers.hook: Click their order link and note what it is: a survey form, a DM request or a payment link with no menu.
openers.linkLine: A weekly meal order with real totals: {demo-link}

openers.line: This week's meal prep menu goes up as a story and vanishes before half your customers check. A weekly menu page would be there whenever they're ready to order.
openers.hook: Watch for the weekly menu story or a highlight called 'menu'. Note the day it goes up.
openers.linkLine: A weekly meal menu that stays up: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your meal prep site on my phone and the menu and order button didn't fit the screen. Meal orders get placed on a phone on Sunday night.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same meal prep site, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your regulars reorder their meal prep by hand every week. A subscription with skip and pause would keep them on without you chasing anyone on Sunday.
openers.hook: Look for posts reminding people to order, or comments like 'same as last week please'. Note one.
openers.linkLine: Weekly meal plans with skip and pause: {demo-link}

openers.line: January is when people search for weekly meal prep to stick to their resolutions. A meal plan page with a clear first-week offer catches them before February.
openers.hook: Use this from late November to January. Check for last year's January posts or offers.
openers.linkLine: A January meal plan page, ready to go: {demo-link}

openers.line: People keep asking in your comments when the meal order deadline is. Every one of those questions is a customer who almost missed this week.
openers.hook: Find comments like 'is it too late to order' or 'when's the cut-off'. Quote one.
openers.linkLine: A meal order cut-off nobody can miss: {demo-link}

openers.line: Under your recent meal prep posts, people keep asking whether you deliver to their neighbourhood. A zone map with delivery windows answers that before they scroll away.
openers.hook: Count 'do you deliver to' comments on recent posts. Note one neighbourhood name.
openers.linkLine: Meal delivery zones on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring kitchen help for the meal prep days. Good cooks check whether a kitchen looks busy and organised before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring story or a 'join the kitchen' post. Note the role and the date.
openers.linkLine: A meal prep site with a join-the-kitchen section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your meals get picked up at a gym, and nothing online explains how that works. A pickup page with days and times would let the gym's members order without asking.
openers.hook: Look for posts tagging a gym or studio as a pickup spot. Note the gym only if they tagged it.
openers.linkLine: A gym pickup page for your meals: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews talk about meals that actually taste good on day four, which is the whole worry with meal prep. That belongs next to the order button.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about taste, portions or convenience. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your meal prep reviews next to the menu: {demo-link}

openers.line: Holiday dinner parties are when people look for a private chef. A page with sample menus and a booking step catches them before the calendars fill.
openers.hook: Use this from October to early December. Look for any private chef dinner posts from last season.
openers.linkLine: Private chef dinners, ready to book for the holidays: {demo-link}

openers.line: People keep asking how much protein is in your meals. Macro labels on the meal prep menu answer that and help the gym crowd pick a plan.
openers.hook: Find comments asking about protein, calories or carbs. Never estimate macros yourself; the chef supplies every number.
openers.linkLine: A meal menu with the chef's macro labels: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your private chef clients all come from word of mouth. When a family moves away, the next household looking for a personal chef searches online first.
openers.hook: Look for posts thanking a client family or reviews mentioning a referral. Quote one without names.
openers.linkLine: Where a new private chef client would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted looks like a meal people would happily eat on a Wednesday at their desk. It should be the first thing on the weekly menu page.
openers.hook: Pick their newest meal or dinner post and name it exactly: the dish and the plan or event it was for.

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted looks like a meal people would actually look forward to midweek.

I looked for a way to order a week of meals from {Business Name} and only found the weekly story and a DM request. I put together a sample meal prep page with this week's menu, the order cut-off, delivery zones and a weekly plan with skip and pause, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case this got lost on a prep day. Here's the sample meal prep page for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has the weekly menu, a cut-off countdown, delivery zones, subscriptions with skip and pause, and a private chef booking page. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for meal prep kitchens and private chefs here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"No problem, prep days are long. Short version: I built a sample page for {Business Name} with your weekly menu, an order cut-off, delivery zones and subscriptions with skip and pause, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and weekly menu updates. For a meal prep business like yours I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"A handful of customers moving to a weekly plan covers it. Can I walk you through it for ten minutes on a day you're not cooking?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and the weekly menu and cut-off go live first."

objections.objection: My customers just DM me their orders.
objections.handler: "That works until you have to total thirty DMs on a Thursday night. The order page totals it, charges it and hands you one prep list."
"That's the point of the weekly menu page. You update it from your phone in a few minutes, and the cut-off countdown resets itself."

objections.objection: I'm a private chef, I don't need a menu online.
objections.handler: "You don't need a menu. You need sample dinners, how bookings work and a consultation step, so a new family trusts you before they let you into their kitchen."
"Then subscriptions help you plan to that capacity. You know your numbers before you shop, and a waitlist holds the next customers."

objections.objection: I use a payment link and that's enough.
objections.handler: "Keep the payment account. The site adds what the link can't: the menu, the cut-off, delivery zones and the weekly plan that renews without you asking."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's a weekly menu, subscriptions and delivery zones. A few weekly plans cover it."

email.subject: Weekly meal order page for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for meal prep businesses and private chefs in {City}, and I put together a sample weekly order page for {Business Name}. I'll text you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} meal prep demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to keep it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — January is when people sign up for weekly meal prep, and holiday dinner parties are when they look for a private chef. Both are coming. Thought of you.

The sample page is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a few weeks of one customer's standing order, not to a month of total sales. That's how a meal prepper measures money.
Subscriptions with skip and pause are the core of the site. Price the ordering logic, not the number of pages.
Price delivery zones by how many zones and windows there are. A single pickup point is quick; five zones with time slots is real work.
Private chef sites price on trust content: sample menus, process and a consultation step. They need fewer pages and more care.
Macro labels are priced per menu template, and the chef supplies every number. Never calculate them for the client.
Sell January plan pages in November and holiday dinner party pages in September.

whatElseYouSell.name: Weekly meal photo session
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One session shooting the core meals in their containers and plated gives the weekly menu real pictures that match what arrives in the bag."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on a prep day when the core meals are already cooked.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for the meal prep kitchen
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "This week's meals and delivery areas on your Google profile every week, so people searching for meal prep near them see you're cooking."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after the first meal week
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After a new customer's first week of meals, they get a short text asking how it went, while they're deciding whether to reorder."

whatElseYouSell.name: January meal plan campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A January push for weekly meal plans with a first-week offer, on the site and in your stories, when people are looking for exactly this."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in November, run from late December to the end of January.

whatElseYouSell.name: Gym and studio partner flyer kit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A front-desk flyer and a counter card with a code to order meal prep for pickup at that gym, so members order without asking the trainers."

whatElseYouSell.name: Cooler bag and container label artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Labels with the meal name, date, reheating code and your brand, plus a cooler bag design, so every delivery looks like the meal prep business it is."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once the reheating guide is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Holiday dinner party push for private chefs
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "An autumn push for private chef holiday dinners, with sample menus and a booking step, before the December calendar fills."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in September, run from October to early December.

withoutAI.route: The gyms where the meals are picked up
withoutAI.whoPays: The gym owner, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The gym that hosts your meal pickups has a class schedule nobody can find on a phone. The meal prep owner can introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Gyms and meal preppers share customers. A partner the gym owner already trusts gets you in.

withoutAI.route: Personal trainers and nutrition coaches who refer
withoutAI.whoPays: Each trainer or coach, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The trainers who send clients to your meal plans book sessions by DM. They need the same clear booking page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Trainers refer meal prep and meal prep refers trainers. The circle is tight and the introduction is warm.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The shared kitchen where you prep meals rents hours to other cooks with no page showing rates or open times. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Shared kitchens need renters. A tenant who preps there weekly is the best introduction.

withoutAI.route: The farm that supplies their produce
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The farm behind your meal prep vegetables sells a weekly box with a paper sign-up. A customer who features them gets you a meeting."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Small farms sell to cooks and households and need a sign-up page. The meal prepper is a steady, trusted buyer.

withoutAI.route: The wine shop that pairs the chef's dinners
withoutAI.whoPays: The wine shop, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The wine shop that pairs bottles for your private chef dinners has no events or tasting page. The chef can make the introduction."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Wine shops run tastings and need sign-ups. The private chef sends them customers already.

withoutAI.whoPays: Each doula practice, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The doulas who recommend your meal plans to new parents book clients by email. They need a clear services page too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: New-parent services refer meal prep constantly. Same households, same trust, a template that carries over.

withAI.route: Membership question assistant for the gym
withAI.pitchLine: "Prospective members ask about classes, prices and trial passes at night, and the gym's assistant answers from its own schedule, meal prep pickup included."
withAI.whyItWorks: Gyms lose trial sign-ups to slow replies. The meal prep client already shares their members.

withAI.route: Client check-in assistant for the trainer
withAI.pitchLine: "Training clients get a weekly check-in message and the trainer gets a summary, with a nudge to reorder meals from the partner kitchen."
withAI.whyItWorks: Trainers struggle to keep clients accountable between sessions. A small monthly tool is easy to justify.

withAI.route: Renter enquiry assistant for the shared kitchen
withAI.pitchLine: "Caterers and bakers ask about hourly rates, equipment and storage, and the shared kitchen's assistant answers and books a walkthrough."
withAI.whyItWorks: Empty kitchen hours cost the owner money. The meal prep tenant can vouch for the need.

withAI.route: Farm box sign-up and swap assistant
withAI.pitchLine: "Households sign up for the farm's weekly box and ask to swap or skip, and the farm gets one clean packing list each week."
withAI.whyItWorks: Farm box programs run on spreadsheets and texts. The meal prep client already orders from them every week.

withAI.route: Pairing suggester for the wine shop
withAI.pitchLine: "Customers enter what they're cooking, or the private chef's menu, and get bottles the shop actually stocks."
withAI.whyItWorks: Pairing questions are the shop's most common conversation. A tool that answers them sells bottles at home too.

withAI.route: Enquiry assistant for the doula practice
withAI.pitchLine: "Expecting parents ask about services and availability and get answers from the practice's own information, with a consult link and the partner meal prep plan for after the birth."
withAI.whyItWorks: Doulas field enquiries while with clients. The meal prep client already shares their families.

softwareAI.name: Order cut-off reminder texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The day before the meal order cut-off, regulars who haven't ordered get a short text with this week's menu, so fewer weeks get missed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: At build or day 14. Needs the cut-off day and time and the customer list with phone numbers.

softwareAI.name: Weekly meal subscriptions with skip and pause
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers pick meals per week once, skip a week for travel or pause for a month, and the card is charged on schedule without you chasing anyone."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 14, once they mention reordering by hand. Needs plan sizes, per-meal prices and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Delivery route planner by zone
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each delivery day the meal bags are sorted into a route by zone and window, so the driver stops crisscrossing town with a cooler."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, when they add a second delivery day or a driver. Needs the zone map and addresses from orders.

softwareAI.name: Meal menu and cut-off answers in DMs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "'What's on the menu this week' and 'do you deliver to my area' get answered from this week's meals and the zone map, with the order link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the weekly menu and zones kept current. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: On-the-way delivery texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers get a text when their meal bag is on the way and when it's dropped, so nobody leaves a week of food on a hot porch."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, after the route planner. Needs delivery routes and customer phone numbers.

softwareAI.name: Kitchen production sheet by meal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The moment the cut-off passes, the kitchen gets one prep sheet: how many of each meal, portion sizes and swaps, instead of totalling orders by hand."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs weekly ordering live and the recipes named.

softwareAI.name: Private chef menu proposal drafter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A family describes the dinner party, guest count and dislikes, and the private chef opens a drafted menu proposal from their own dishes to edit and send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, for private chefs. Needs past menus and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Customer taste and dislike profiles
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every meal prep customer's dislikes and swaps saved on their profile, so the kitchen never sends mushrooms to the person who hates them."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the swaps they currently track in notes or memory.

softwareAI.name: Weekly meal description writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Type the week's meals in a few words and get short, appetite-first menu descriptions and a caption for the weekly post, ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs a few past menus and captions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Failed card retry and payment reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a subscriber's card fails, they get a polite text to update it before the meal prep cut-off, so the kitchen doesn't cook for an unpaid order."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once subscriptions are live. Needs the payment account.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for meal prep
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a subscriber praises the chicken bowl or the plant-based plan, a warm meal prep reply quoting that detail is waiting on your phone to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside the review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Private chef booking with deposit
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Families pick a date for the private chef dinner, enter guests and dislikes, and pay a deposit, so the date is held and the shopping can start."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, for private chefs. Needs their deposit rule, availability and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Meal plan matcher
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New customers answer a few questions about their week and preferences and get a suggested meal plan size and style from your menu, with no health promises."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs plan styles and the owner's rules for who fits which. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Container return reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Subscribers get a reminder to leave last week's meal containers out on delivery day, and the deposit tracker shows who still has them."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, if they run a reusable container program. Needs the deposit rules.

softwareAI.name: Gift meal plans
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Friends and family buy a week of meals for new parents or someone recovering at home, and the recipient picks the delivery week."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, before the holidays. Needs gift plan sizes and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Meal prep phone and text answering
softwareAI.pitchLine: "On prep days, calls and texts about meal plans, delivery zones and private chef dates still get answered and logged for you."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, once they trust the DM answers. Needs menu, zones, plans and policies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Referral credits for subscribers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Subscribers get a meal credit when a friend signs up for a weekly plan with their code, so the gym crowd does the selling."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs subscriptions live and a credit the owner is happy to give.

softwareAI.name: Next week's quantity forecaster
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Before the cut-off, it estimates how many of each meal will sell from subscriptions and past weeks, so the grocery order starts early and less goes to waste."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, with a few months of order history. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Ingredient overlap planner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Draft next week's meal menu and it flags ingredients you can share across dishes, so a case of peppers gets used in three meals, not one."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs recipes with ingredients and supplier pack sizes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Food cost per meal tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See what each meal really costs in ingredients and containers, so the per-meal price on the plan keeps up when chicken prices jump."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs recipes with quantities and current grocery or supplier prices.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise weekly subscriptions for independent meal preppers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every small meal prep kitchen totals DM orders on Thursday night. A weekly menu with cut-off, subscriptions and a prep sheet is a product they'll pay for monthly."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for the workflow. Meal preppers are many and easy to find through gyms.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give every member private chef a sample-menus page and a booking step with deposit, as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Chef associations need visible benefits. A booking page is what most members still lack.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Gym groups' member meal prep program
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer members weekly meal prep pickup at every location from local kitchens, ordered through one page in your app or site."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Gym groups want amenities that keep members. The meal prep client already runs pickup at one of their gyms.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Culinary school private chef launch kits
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Graduates who go private leave with a chef page, sample menus and a booking step. It's a career path you can put in the brochure."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Schools sell outcomes, and private chef work is a common path for their graduates.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every meal prep tenant in your kitchen needs a weekly order page. Offer one template to all of them as part of their rental."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Shared kitchens compete for tenants. A ready storefront is a perk that fills hours.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The employer or its benefits provider
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Employees order subsidised weekly meal prep from vetted local kitchens through one ordering page the HR team controls."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Employers buy perks in bulk. A local meal prep client proves the ordering works.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Vacation rental managers' private chef bookings
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Guests in your rentals ask for a private chef for the big dinner. A booking page with vetted chefs and sample menus sells it before arrival."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Rental managers earn on add-ons and want happy guests. The private chef client is the first one on the page.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Residents ask the concierge for meal delivery and private chefs. A resident page with vetted meal prep and chef partners answers it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: High-end buildings sell amenities. Food services are among the most requested.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Home care agencies' meal add-on page
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Families arranging care ask who can cook for their parent. A meal plan add-on page with a local kitchen gives the agency an answer."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies get the question constantly and want a trusted partner. The meal prep client fits naturally.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Hospital and birth centre new-parent meal partners
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The birth centre or hospital foundation
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "New parents leave with a code for a gift meal plan from a local kitchen. A partner page makes the referral easy for staff."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Birth centres look for meaningful extras. Meal plans for new parents are an easy yes, with no health claims needed.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label meal prep ordering for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency picks up meal prep clients and can't build subscriptions. License my weekly menu and cut-off template."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell them the ordering logic you've already built.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: One meal prep kitchen per gym cluster, metro by metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New meal prep clients in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one meal prep kitchen per gym cluster in {City}. The gyms in the next metro have their own preppers still taking DMs."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Meal prep markets form around gyms and delivery zones. Non-competing clusters let you reuse the template and the proof.

upsellLadder.offer: Meal prep site plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The meal prep site and the care plan go on one contract, so next week's menu is a quick update, not a project."

upsellLadder.offer: Weekly meal subscriptions with skip and pause
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention regulars who reorder the same meals by DM every week.
upsellLadder.line: "Your regulars already order the same meals weekly. A subscription makes it automatic for both of you."

upsellLadder.offer: Review requests after the first meal week
upsellLadder.trigger: New customers are finishing their first week of meals with no review follow-up.
upsellLadder.line: "Ask new meal customers how week one went, right when they're deciding to reorder."

upsellLadder.trigger: They add a second delivery day, a new zone or a driver.
upsellLadder.line: "A second delivery day is where the meal routes get messy. Let's sort them by zone automatically."
